statusText: Mapped policy state: BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. Tail 26% has crossed out of the 20-24 watch band into the 25-34 elevated band.
recommendation: The retracement mechanism that held Tail at 24 for the previous three hours has failed. The roughly 57-point bounce off 30,564.25 did not hold; NQ extended to a fifth successive Globex lower low at 30,531.00 and now trades 30,542.25 to 30,549.25, within 18 points of that extreme and 1.10% below the 30,889.25 settlement. Repeated extension after a failed retracement, combined with NQ holding near its session low, is the observed structure this score is designed to flag, and it now sits alongside three independent amplifiers: VIX at 16.36 is up 10.03% from Friday's 14.87, the 10-year yield has reached 5.23% and the 2-year 4.93%, and Brent has risen 3.4% to about $100.8 after the Strait of Hormuz truce proposal was rejected. Tail therefore moves to 26 and the mapped policy state becomes BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES. It stays at the low end of the elevated band rather than higher because the repricing remains narrow: E-mini S&P futures are down 0.55% against the Nasdaq-100's 1.10%, the DAX is unchanged at 25,398.46, and the full 389.75-point Globex range is 1.26% of settle across roughly fourteen hours, which is directional drift rather than a violent one-way path. The identified checkpoint remains the 13:00Z-16:00Z window covering the 13:30Z cash open and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release, where U.S. and, with Taiwan closed, Taiwanese chipmakers have still not priced the OpenAI training pause.
headline: NQ extends to a fifth Globex lower low at 30,531.00 after the prior bounce fails and holds within 18 points of it; VIX +10.03% at 16.36, a 5.23% 10-year and Brent +3.4% lift Tail to 26 and the state to BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures trade at 30,549.25 on the 09:15Z Yahoo Finance quote and 30,542.25 on the 09:16Z Investing.com quote, 340.00 to 347.00 points and 1.10% to 1.12% below Friday's 30,889.25 settlement. Both feeds show a session low of 30,531.00, roughly 33 points beneath the 30,564.25 low that was current at the previous assessment, and the session high of 30,920.75 puts the full Globex range at 389.75 points.

The decisive change since the previous hour is the behaviour of the retracement, not the new low itself. An hour ago price had recovered about 57 points off its low and was not pinned to the extreme, which was the specific reason Tail was held at 24. That bounce has now failed: price extended a further 33 points and currently sits 11.25 to 18.25 points above the session low. Repeated extension after a failed retracement, with NQ holding near its session extreme, is the observed price-path structure the Tail score exists to flag, and it is the reason Tail crosses into the 25-34 elevated band at 26 rather than holding in the watch band.

Three independent cross-asset amplifiers are aligned with that structure. The VIX has risen 10.03% to 16.36 from Friday's 14.87 close, its day range of 16.10 to 16.36 showing no intraday decay in the volatility bid. The U.S. 10-year yield has reached 5.23%, up about 7 basis points and its highest level since July 2007, with the 2-year at 4.93%. Brent crude has risen 3.40% to 100.75 and 3.52% to 100.87 on two independent feeds from a 97.44 close, after the seven-day truce proposal that would have reopened the Strait of Hormuz was rejected.

The counterweight is breadth, and it is why the score stays at the low end of the elevated band. E-mini S&P futures are down 0.55%, half the Nasdaq-100's 1.10%, and the DAX is unchanged at 25,398.46 against a 25,396.22 close after giving back an earlier gain. The Globex range of 389.75 points is 1.26% of settle across roughly fourteen hours, which is directional drift rather than the violent repricing a much higher Tail would describe. The weakness remains a concentrated AI and semiconductor de-rating, driven by OpenAI's pause of training, evaluation and tool-use inference for its most capable models following a security incident with an internal research model. Asian memory names carried the move, with SK Hynix down 4.8% and Samsung Electronics 4.6%, the KOSPI down 2.3% and the CSI 300 down 2%, while Taiwan was closed for a holiday so TSMC and its supply chain have not traded the news at all.

That closure matters for the forecast path. The published horizon places its peak Tail of 30 on the 14:00Z hour, covering post-open continuation risk and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release, and sets a second local peak of 25 on the 01:00Z hour when Taiwan reopens and prices the pause for the first time. Both are conditional risks, not observations. Stress is raised to 84 and peaks at 86 in the danger window, carrying the oil premium, the highest 10-year yield since 2007 and an unresolved AI-capex question into a week that holds JOLTS and CB Consumer Confidence on Tuesday, core PCE and ADP on Wednesday, ISM Manufacturing on Thursday and payrolls on Friday. Confidence is 85: two independent price feeds agree on the level, the session low and the settlement, and the VIX, yield, oil and calendar evidence is current and verified. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 05:58Z, is therefore about three and a half hours old and outside the 90-minute freshness limit, and its collectionStatus is partial with the futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it contributed nothing to this assessment.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail held at 7-8% through the Sunday European and U.S. hours, drifted to 9-14% across the Globex reopen while Stress climbed from 62% to 76%, eased to 9-12% between 00:00Z and 02:00Z, then stepped to 21% at 03:00Z when NQ first took out Friday's low, 22% at 04:00Z, back to 21% at 05:00Z and up to 24% for the three hours from 06:00Z to 08:00Z as successive overnight lows broke. Dominant mode was normal for eighteen of the twenty-four hours, mixed at 02:00Z and 05:00Z and trend-down at 03:00Z, 04:00Z, 06:00Z, 07:00Z and 08:00Z. Eighteen hours mapped to EA_ON and the most recent six to WATCH.
outlookSummary: The published horizon runs from the 09:00Z hour on 28 September through 08:00Z on 29 September. Tail opens in the 25-34 elevated band and stays there for eleven of the twenty-four hours, peaking at 30% on the 14:00Z hour that covers post-open continuation risk and the 14:30Z Dallas Fed Manufacturing release. A second local peak of 25% falls on the 01:00Z hour, when Taiwan reopens from its holiday and TSMC prices the OpenAI training pause for the first time. Tail returns to the 20-24 watch band for the U.S. afternoon and most of the Asian session, and drops to 18% in the low band only for the 21:00Z CME maintenance break, when no meaningful price discovery exists. Stress holds between 78% and 86% throughout, reflecting the Hormuz oil premium with Brent near $100.8, a 10-year yield at its highest since July 2007 and an unresolved AI-capex question ahead of a week carrying JOLTS, CB Consumer Confidence, ADP, core PCE, ISM Manufacturing and payrolls. Confidence starts at 85% on two agreeing current price feeds and decays to 70-71% across the far edge of the horizon.
